titre: Opening a bank account for my teenager
resume: At what age, with which card, the parents' consent (including separated parents) and the list of documents to bring to the bank so you don't make the trip for nothing.
aQuoiCaSert: An account in your teenager's name lets them receive pocket money or wages from a part-time job, and learn to manage a budget with a card suited to their age. A minor who is not emancipated cannot open an account alone: their legal representatives, usually their parents, act on their behalf. The parents remain responsible for managing this money.
quiEstConcerne: Parents of a teenager aged 12 to 17 who want to open an account or a savings account with a card for them.
Separated parents who need to agree on opening the child's account or on the transactions made on it.
aSavoir: From birth, the parents can open an account in the child's name, without the child's consent.
From age 12: with your consent, the young person can request a Livret jeune (a youth savings account) and make deposits and withdrawals. Withdrawals can be limited and your signature is required.
From age 16: with your permission, they can open a bank account with a card and checkbook, and withdraw money freely.
Opening an account is free, but the bank may charge account or card fees: ask for the price information before signing.
Parents may only use the child's money for expenses that directly concern the child (education, upkeep). When the child turns 16, they must account to the child for this use.

Parents who share parental authority, even if separated: changing a minor's account is an act of disposal that requires both parents' agreement (Cour de cassation, France's highest court, June 12, 2025, no. 24-13.604). The bank may therefore ask for both signatures.
If you hold parental authority alone by court decision, bring that decision to the bank.

documents.detail: ID card or passport. If it has expired or been lost, get a new one from the town hall (mairie) first.
Valid ID card, passport or residence permit, with photo.
Often requested when both parents hold parental authority. Ask the bank whether they need to come and sign.

documents.libelle: Family record book (livret de famille) or the child's birth certificate showing parentage
documents.detail: Proves you are the parents. Free birth certificate online or from the town hall where the child was born.
Tax notice, rent receipt, water or electricity bill. If someone is housing you, the bank may ask for a certificate of accommodation.

documents.libelle: Court decision or agreement on parental authority (copy)
documents.detail: If you hold parental authority alone or if a decision sets out the child's situation.

documents.libelle: Written, signed consent from the other parent
documents.detail: If the other parent cannot come and the bank accepts it: dated, signed letter, with a copy of their ID document.

documents.libelle: Account opening contract and fee terms
documents.detail: Given at signing. Keep them to keep track of fees and card limits.

etapes.titre: Choose the right product for their age
etapes.detail: Livret jeune from age 12, an account with a card and checkbook from age 16 with your permission. Compare the fees and limits.

etapes.titre: Talk it over with the other parent
etapes.detail: If you share parental authority, agree on the product, the card and the limits. A written agreement avoids deadlocks.

etapes.titre: Book an appointment at the bank
etapes.detail: Ask for the exact list of documents and whether both parents and the teenager must be present.

Original ID of the teenager and of each parent, family record book or birth certificate, recent proof of address, judgment or agreement if you are separated, written consent of the other parent if absent.

etapes.titre: Set up the card and limits
etapes.detail: Ask the bank for a card that checks the balance at each payment if you want to avoid any overdraft, and set limits.

etapes.titre: Store the contract in the Vault
etapes.detail: With the bank details (RIB) and the price information.

ou.detail: Branch or online bank: offers and required documents vary from one bank to another.

In the overseas departments, the IEDOM (Institut d'émission des départements d'outre-mer, the overseas central bank institute) handles the right to a bank account if a bank refuses to open an account.
